Sony Ends Physical PlayStation Games in 2028 — Nintendo's About to WIN

short // Jul 9, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

PlayStation thinks it's too big for its britches. Too big to fail.

Sony just confirmed it: starting January 2028, new PlayStation games go all-digital. No discs. No case on the shelf. No "hey, borrow this for the weekend." And I don't think Sony thought this all the way through.

My money's on a new leader in town, and I'm betting on Nintendo. This is their time to move up, and I'm all for it.

You don't own it

Any company that's for legal ownership of what a consumer buys, I'm for it. Why should I give my money to a company that can take it away anytime it wants?

When you buy a digital game, you're buying permission to play it, and that permission belongs to whoever runs the store. Imagine a world where your games get shut down and they're all digital. You can't play them. That's kind of scary.

And it's not a what-if. They already did it with movies: digital movie libraries have lost titles when licensing deals ran out. A disc never asked you to trust anybody. It worked because it was in your hand.

The part nobody's talking about: retail bleeds too

This isn't just hurting customers. It's hurting the retail side, too. Think about the stores that sell physical games:

  • GameStop
  • Walmart
  • Target
  • Best Buy

If they can't sell physical PlayStation games anymore, how does the retail side make money off of this? You take a big chunk of profit away from them, and that's going to be a big backlash, too.

And nobody goes into a store for exactly one thing. You come in for a game and leave with a controller, a headset or a gift card. That disc is the reason the rest of the cart happens.

Great margins, shame about the trust

I know it's a money game. No discs means no manufacturing, no shipping, no shelf space and no used market undercutting your price. Sony wants to make as much profit as it can.

But it's really not just screwing us. It's screwing the retail side of it, too. Sony didn't get here on hardware specs alone. It got here on decades of goodwill from players who bought in early and stayed loyal, and goodwill doesn't come back once you've spent it.

Is Sony as a company maybe over? That's where my head's at right now.

Update (September 2026)

Here's where things stand:

  • It's official. Sony announced it on the PlayStation Blog on July 1: physical disc production ends for all new games starting January 2028, and those games will be sold on the PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. Games released on disc before then aren't affected.
  • The backlash was real. "No disc, no buy" flooded Sony's posts, but Sony's CFO has said the company will "cautiously move this forward."
  • Nintendo isn't following. Analysts don't expect Nintendo to change course because of Sony, and according to CBR, boxed games still make up about 38.5% of Nintendo's software sales.

So far, my bet on Nintendo is holding up.

Sources: PlayStation Blog, CNBC, Tom's Hardware, VGC, CBR

Quick answers

Is PlayStation ending physical games? Yes. Sony will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games released starting January 2028.

When does PlayStation go digital-only? January 2028, for new games. Games released on disc before then aren't affected.

Can I still buy PlayStation games at stores after 2028? New games will be sold in digital formats only, on the PlayStation Store and at retailers.

Is Nintendo getting rid of physical games? There's no sign of it. Analysts don't expect Nintendo to follow Sony, and boxed games are still a big part of its sales.

Your turn

Are you Team Sony, or Team Physical? Let me know in the comments.
